title: Introducing others and the verb sein (Das ist ...)
summary: Introduce colleagues and friends, use sein (to be) and all the personal pronouns, and say how old you are.
goals: Use sein in every person: ich bin, du bist, er ist ...
Use the personal pronouns, including the three meanings of sie
Say and ask how old someone is

nicosWeg.title: Nicos Weg A1, chapter 1: Meeting people (Das ist Nico, Nico hat ein Problem)

points: To ask about someone you see: [[Wer ist das?]] (who is that?), then [[Woher kommt er?]], [[Wo wohnt er?]], [[Wie alt ist er?]]
Talking about one person uses [[er]], [[sie]] or [[es]], and the verb ends in -t: [[er kommt]], [[sie wohnt]], [[sie arbeitet]].
A child is [[das Kind]], so it is [[es]]: [[Es wohnt in Berlin.]]
For two or more people, the question becomes [[Wer sind sie?]] and the answer [[Das sind ...]]. Then [[sie]] (they) takes -en: [[Sie kommen aus Italien.]]
Practice idea from the video: describe a friend, then your parents or a group of friends, with these sentences.
The video asks the ten questions of a first conversation, each in a polite and an informal version.
Polite questions use [[Sie]] and a verb ending in -en ([[Wie heißen Sie?]]); informal ones use [[du]] and -st ([[Wie heißt du?]]).
'Your' changes too: [[Ihr]] (polite) and [[dein]] (informal): [[Wie ist Ihr Familienname?]], [[Was sind deine Hobbys?]]
[[sprechen]] changes its vowel with du: [[Welche Sprachen sprichst du?]]
Yes/no questions start with the verb: [[Sind Sie verheiratet?]], [[Haben Sie Kinder?]]
Saying no: [[nicht]] before an adjective ([[Ich bin nicht verheiratet.]]), [[keine]] before a noun ([[Ich habe keine Kinder.]]).

phrases.en: What do you do for a living? (informal)

points: A personal pronoun replaces a noun, so you don't repeat it. Which one you pick depends on the person (I, you, he/she), singular or plural, and for 'you' on formal or informal.
First person: [[ich]], plural [[wir]]: [[Ich wohne in New York.]], [[Wir wohnen in New York.]]
Informal 'you' goes with first names: [[du]] for one person, [[ihr]] for several: [[Max, wo wohnst du?]], [[Lena und Peter, wo wohnt ihr?]]
Polite 'you' is [[Sie]] for one person and for several, always with a capital S: [[Herr Müller, wo wohnen Sie?]]

Third person: [[er]] (masculine), [[sie]] (feminine), [[es]] (neuter), plural [[sie]]. They stand for things too: [[Das ist mein Buch. Es ist alt.]] This [[sie]] takes a capital only at the start of a sentence.

phrases.de: Lena und Peter, wo wohnt ihr?
phrases.en: Lena and Peter, where do you live?
Mr Müller, where do you live?

phrases.de: Das ist Thomas. Er wohnt in London.
phrases.en: This is Thomas. He lives in London.

phrases.de: Das ist mein Buch. Es ist alt.
phrases.en: This is my book. It's old.

phrases.de: Katrin und Peter wohnen in Hamburg.
phrases.en: Katrin and Peter live in Hamburg.

points: [[haben]] and [[sein]] are the two most important verbs: main verbs now, and later the helpers of the past tense.
[[haben]]: [[ich habe]], [[du hast]], [[er hat]], [[wir haben]], [[ihr habt]], [[sie haben]]. Its endings are the ones most verbs use; only du and er lose the b.
[[sein]] has no pattern, so learn it as it is: [[ich bin]], [[du bist]], [[er ist]], [[wir sind]], [[ihr seid]], [[sie sind]].

When the subject is a name or a noun, conjugate as for the pronoun that could replace it: [[Eva]] is [[sie]], so [[Eva hat eine Tochter.]] [[Meine Eltern]] are [[sie]] (they), so [[Meine Eltern haben einen Hund.]]

phrases.de: Frau Schmidt, sind Sie zu Hause?
phrases.en: Ms Schmidt, are you at home?

points: There are four sie's. With a capital S: polite 'you', for one person or several. With a small s: 'she' and 'they'.
The verb tells you which: polite [[Sie]] and [[sie]] (they) take -en ([[Sie wohnen]], [[sie wohnen]]); [[sie]] (she) takes -t ([[sie wohnt]]).
Polite [[Sie]] keeps its capital everywhere in the sentence. [[sie]] (she, they) gets a capital only at the start of a sentence.
As an object (accusative) they all stay the same: [[Herr Schmidt, ich besuche Sie heute.]], [[Ich besuche sie heute.]] In the dative they change: [[Ihnen]], [[ihr]], [[ihnen]].
Use [[Sie]] with people you don't know, at offices and with authorities, and to be polite; otherwise [[du]].

phrases.en: Mr Müller, where do you live?

phrases.de: Herr und Frau Müller, wo wohnen Sie?
phrases.en: Mr and Mrs Müller, where do you live?

phrases.de: Das ist Lena. Heute ist sie nicht zu Hause.
phrases.en: This is Lena. Today she isn't at home.

phrases.de: Das ist Mila. Sie ist meine Schwester.
phrases.en: This is Mila. She's my sister.

phrases.de: Das sind Max und Thomas. Morgen schreiben sie einen Test.
phrases.en: These are Max and Thomas. Tomorrow they're writing a test.

phrases.de: Herr Schmidt, ich besuche Sie heute.
phrases.en: Mr Schmidt, I'll visit you today.
Ms Weber, where are you from?

sections.title: Introducing someone
sections.text:
Point and say [[Das ist ...]]: [[Das ist Anna.]] [[Das ist mein Kollege Aram.]] The usual answer is [[Freut mich!]] (nice to meet you) or simply [[Hallo!]].

With people you call [[Sie]], use [[Herr]] or [[Frau]] plus the surname: [[Herr Weber]], [[Frau Schmidt]]. First names usually go with [[du]].

For a woman it is [[meine]]: [[Das ist meine Kollegin.]] (the -e comes with die words; Unit 2, lesson 4 explains). Careful with [[Freund]] and [[Freundin]]: [[mein Freund]] and [[meine Freundin]] often mean boyfriend and girlfriend. For just a friend, say [[ein Freund von mir]] or [[eine Freundin von mir]] (a fixed phrase for now; [[mir]] comes in Unit 6).

sections.title: sein (to be): learn it by heart

sections.text:
Russian drops 'to be' in the present (Я студент), but German never does: [[Ich bin Student.]]

Armenian keeps it too, but at the **end**: Ես ուսանող եմ. German puts it in **second** place: [[Ich bin Student.]] Watch the position.

[[sie]] has three meanings: she, they, and (with a capital S) polite you. The verb tells you which: [[sie ist]] = she is, [[sie sind]] = they are, [[Sie sind]] = you are (polite). At the start of a sentence all three are capitalized, so only the verb and the context help.

items.de: Wer ist das? - Das ist Frau Schmidt. Sie ist neu hier.
items.en: Who is that? - That's Ms Schmidt. She's new here.

sections.text: Age works like Armenian: 'I am thirty' - [[Ich bin dreißig.]], Ես երեսուն տարեկան եմ. Russian uses a different structure (Мне тридцать лет), so don't translate from Russian here.

items.question: A colleague introduces you to Anna. What do you say?
items.explanation: Freut mich! = Nice to meet you!
Das ist ... introduces someone. The verb ist is in second place.
sie ist = she is. At the start of the sentence: Sie ist ...
